Parser golden files are gitignored, so `go test ./parser/...` cannot validate trees in a fresh checkout; the fix agent validated trees by generating goldens from main in a worktree and running the branch against them (all 5083 pass).

hypotheses.title: Lexer allocates fresh trivia slice, minutiae and one-element node list for every token, even for the ubiquitous single-space/newline trivia
hypotheses.issue: In stage 1 every token goes through parser/lexer.go getLeadingTrivia and processTrailingTrivia. (1) Both allocate a new []st.STNode buffer per token (getLeadingTrivia re-makes l.context.leadingTriviaList after handing the old backing array to st.CreateNodeList; processTrailingTrivia makes a cap-1 slice before knowing if trivia exists) — ~4.4M wasted slices on the reproducer since most leading trivia is empty. (2) For the overwhelmingly common trivia — exactly one space, or exactly "\n" — each token additionally allocates a new STMinutiae (processWhitespaces/processEndOfLine -> st.CreateMinutiae) and a new one-element STNodeList (st.CreateNodeList). These are retained in the green tree for the whole compilation, so they inflate peak RSS and GC work. Green nodes carry no parent/position (those live in per-instance facades) and are never mutated after construction (all modifiers build copies), so identical trivia can be shared like emptyNodeList already is. Same patterns exist in documentation_lexer.go and xml_lexer.go. Measured on the reproducer (2.36M tokens): trivia handling ~8.9M of 40M heap objects; Parse stage ~1.2s of ~6.2s total; max RSS ~3.9GB.

reproducer.generator:
# Generates a token-heavy Ballerina file: F functions x S statements, each ~16 tokens with
# single-space trailing trivia, to expose per-token trivia allocations in the lexer.
import sys
F = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 200
S = int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 500
o = ["import ballerina/io;", ""]
for f in range(F):
    o.append(f"function f{f}(int a, int b, int c) returns int {{")
    o.append("    int s = 0;")
    for k in range(S):
        o.append(f"    s = s + a * ( b - {k} ) + c % 7 - ( a + {k} ) ;")
    o.append("    return s;")
    o.append("}")
o.append("public function main() {")
o.append("    int t = 0;")
for f in range(F):
    o.append(f"    t = t + f{f}(1, 2, 3);")
o.append("    io:println(t);")
o.append("}")
print("\n".join(o))
reproducer.command: python3 gen_tokens.py 200 500 > tokens.bal && ./bin/benchmark --mode time --runs 5 --warmup 1 main <branch> tokens.bal (and --mode memory); stage view: go run ./cli/cmd run --stats tokens.bal | grep -E '^  (Parse|AST Build|Total)'

hypotheses.fix_approach: Two parts in parser/. (a) Keep reusable scratch buffers for leading and trailing trivia in lexerContext; a helper takeTriviaList returns the shared empty list when the buffer is empty, otherwise builds the list from an exact-size slices.Clone and truncates the buffer for reuse (removes the per-token make). (b) At package init build shared immutable WHITESPACE_MINUTIAE nodes for runs of 1-16 spaces and an END_OF_LINE_MINUTIAE for "\n", each with a shared one-element STNodeList; processWhitespaces/processEndOfLine return the shared minutiae only when the lexeme text matches exactly (tabs, \r\n, longer runs still allocate), and takeTriviaList returns the shared list when the buffer holds exactly one shared minutiae (pointer identity check). Safety: STNodeBase has no parent/position; facades cache children per facade instance; setDiagnostics/ModifyWith/AddAll/CloneWith*InvalidNodeMinutiae all operate on fresh copies; no maps keyed by STNode; pointer-equality uses (st.Replace, diagnostic TextRange) target tokens/expressions, never trivia. Pitfall: part (a) alone is not measurable — the retained per-token minutiae+list nodes dominate. make test and make test-race pass; parser trees identical to main.

notes: Exploration also noted (not pursued): desugar/expression.go hoistAndAddDefaultInvocations copies all preceding args per default-param closure call (O(params^2) per call; 124ms@100 -> 525ms@200 defaults); --stats stage totals are summed across concurrently running modules in multi-module packages; a deeply indented nested-if file panics in birgen with a negative column (likely uint16 width overflow) — possible correctness bug.
